verdict.oneLiner: Reading mail means restricted scopes: domain and brand verification, scope verification taking several weeks, and an annual third-party security assessment. Sending only (gmail.send) avoids the assessment.

steps.title: Copy the Composio callback URL
steps.detail: In Composio: Authentication management → Create Auth Config → Gmail → OAuth2 → Use your own developer credentials. The redirect URI is https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback.

steps.title: Create a Google Cloud project and branding
steps.detail: Create a project, then Google Auth Platform → Get started: app name, support email, Audience: External, contact email, agree to the User Data Policy. Home page, privacy policy and logo can wait until you publish.
takeoverPoints: Agree to the Google API Services User Data Policy

steps.title: Add Gmail scopes and test users
steps.detail: Data Access → add the Gmail scopes. Audience → add test users, including yourself: the project owner isn't a test user automatically.

steps.title: Create the OAuth client
steps.detail: Clients → Create client → Web application. Authorized redirect URI: the Composio callback (exact match), or your own domain's forwarder (see gotchas).
takeoverPoints: Copy the client secret: it's shown only once

steps.title: Paste the client ID and secret into Composio
steps.detail: Copy the client ID and secret into the Composio auth config.

steps.title: Test with a test user
steps.detail: Connect a test account and run one Gmail tool. Test grants expire after 7 days.

steps.title: Verify your domains
steps.detail: Verify the home page, privacy policy and redirect domains in Google Search Console.

steps.title: Draft justifications and record the demo video
steps.detail: Write why each scope is needed and record an unlisted YouTube video of the consent flow and each scope's feature.

steps.title: Publish and submit for verification
steps.detail: Audience → Publish app, then submit brand verification and scope verification.

steps.title: Brand and scope verification
steps.detail: Brand: about 2-3 business days if reviewed manually. Restricted scopes: several weeks, plus the security assessment.

whileYouWait.text: Keep users on Composio managed auth meanwhile.
Use up to 100 test users, re-consenting every 7 days.

gotchas.text: Using Composio's callback adds composio.dev to your authorized domains, and verification needs every authorized domain verified, which you can't do for composio.dev. Plan for your own callback domain that 302-forwards to Composio (the forwarder itself isn't tested yet).
Test-user grants expire after 7 days, so long-running agents break in Testing.
Going to production unverified caps the project at 100 users for its lifetime.
Asking only for gmail.send keeps you out of the restricted-scope security assessment.
Switching from managed auth to your own OAuth app doesn't migrate existing connections: users reconnect, or you import their credentials where supported.
The project owner isn't a test user automatically; add yourself or Gmail scopes fail with 403 access_denied.
Until the app is branded and verified, Google's sign-in screens say "composio.dev", not your app name.

unknowns: CASA fees: Google and the App Defense Alliance don't publish them.
Whether there's a cap on authorized domains per project.
A numeric duration for restricted scope verification (Google says only 'several weeks').
Whether a 302 forwarder on your domain satisfies Google's redirect-domain check end to end (not yet tested).
